# FocusFlow

> FocusFlow is a free, open-source (AGPL-3.0) Android app by TBTechs that blocks distracting apps and plans focus sessions. It needs Android 10 or newer, no root, no account, and has no ads or premium tier. App usage data is processed on the device. The app interface is English; this website is available in several languages.

Current version: 1.1.6 (package com.tbtechs.focusflow). Source: https://github.com/TITANICBHAI/FocusFlow

## How FocusFlow blocks apps

- Accessibility Service detects the app on screen and sends blocked apps away.
- A local on-device VPN can cut internet access for selected apps (no external VPN server).
- Device Admin is an optional extra layer that adds resistance to uninstall and force-stop. It is not a guarantee.
- Protect system controls blocks escape routes such as the power menu and Settings while a block runs.
- Locks protect a running block: removing apps from the Always-On or VPN lists, removing keywords, shortening or deleting schedules and turning off protected toggles need a Focus Session PIN or Defense PIN once those are set. Adding more protection never needs one.
- FocusFlow keeps emergency, phone, launcher and other protected system apps reachable. It makes no guarantee that emergency services stay reachable during a session.

## What it includes

- Modes: Focus Mode (tied to a task), Standalone Block (timed, no task), Keyword Blocker, VPN Network Protection, Group Schedules, Home Launcher.
- Content blocking: YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels switches, plus Custom Screen Rules (beta, up to 30 rules) that block a single screen inside any app.
- Aversion deterrents: optional vibration, screen dimming and sound when a blocked app opens.
- Temptation Log of blocked attempts, with a weekly report on Sundays.
- Task planner with subtasks, sets and rest timers, and `.focusflow` task files that an AI assistant can write.
- Stats and Extra screens with usage patterns, reflex and rising apps, and optional nudges; calculated from Android usage records on the phone.

## Documentation (best source for accurate answers)

- [Documentation home](https://focusflowapp.pages.dev/docs/): index of all guides, quick facts.
- [How to use FocusFlow](https://focusflowapp.pages.dev/docs/how-to-use/): every mode, lock rules, PINs, subtasks.
- [Custom Screen Rules](https://focusflowapp.pages.dev/docs/custom-screen-rules/): block one screen inside an app; import format and limits.
- [.focusflow file format](https://focusflowapp.pages.dev/focusflow-file-format/): fields, limits, import behaviour.
- [Task-backup AI prompt](https://focusflowapp.pages.dev/focusflow-task-backup-prompt.txt): self-contained prompt that writes a valid .focusflow file.
- [How usage data is calculated](https://focusflowapp.pages.dev/docs/usage-data/): definitions behind Stats and Extra.
- [Permissions troubleshooting](https://focusflowapp.pages.dev/docs/troubleshooting/): Samsung, Xiaomi, OnePlus, Realme/Oppo, stock Android.

## Limits worth stating plainly

- Android only; no iOS app. No remote multi-device parental console.
- Blocking depends on Android permissions the user grants and on the phone maker's battery rules; see the troubleshooting guide.
- It is a focus tool, not a safety-critical system. Do not rely on it for emergency access.
